+package chi
+
+import (
+	"net/http"
+	"sort"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// CORSOptions configures the built-in CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)
+// support. Use DefaultCORSOptions as the starting point and change what
+// differs.
+type CORSOptions struct {
+	// AllowOrigin is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Origin. An empty
+	// value means "*".
+	AllowOrigin string
+
+	// AllowMethods is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Methods on a
+	// preflight response. When it is empty the methods that have a handler
+	// on the requested path are used, so the header always matches the
+	// routes of the router.
+	AllowMethods []string
+
+	// AllowHeaders is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Headers on a
+	// preflight response. When it is empty the headers the browser asked
+	// for in Access-Control-Request-Headers are allowed.
+	AllowHeaders []string
+
+	// ExposeHeaders is the value of Access-Control-Expose-Headers: the
+	// response headers a browser may show to the calling script.
+	ExposeHeaders []string
+
+	// MaxAge is how many seconds a browser may cache a preflight response
+	// (Access-Control-Max-Age). Zero leaves the header out.
+	MaxAge int
+
+	// AllowCredentials sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. Browsers
+	// refuse a wildcard origin together with credentials, so with the
+	// wildcard origin the request's own Origin is answered instead.
+	AllowCredentials bool
+}
+
+// DefaultCORSOptions returns the options EnableCORS uses: any origin, the
+// headers most APIs need and a preflight cache of one hour. The allowed
+// methods are left empty so they follow the routes.
+func DefaultCORSOptions() CORSOptions {
+	return CORSOptions{
+		AllowOrigin: "*",
+		AllowHeaders: []string{
+			"Accept",
+			"Authorization",
+			"Content-Type",
+			"X-CSRF-Token",
+			"X-Requested-With",
+		},
+		MaxAge: 3600,
+	}
+}
+
+// corsFallbackMethods answers a preflight when no route was found for the
+// path and the options name no methods.
+var corsFallbackMethods = []string{
+	http.MethodGet, http.MethodHead, http.MethodPost,
+	http.MethodPut, http.MethodPatch, http.MethodDelete, http.MethodOptions,
+}
+
+// CORS returns a middleware that sets the CORS response headers on every
+// response and answers a preflight request (an OPTIONS request carrying
+// Access-Control-Request-Method) itself with 204 No Content, without calling
+// the next handler.
+//
+// Used with Mux.Use it runs before routing, so the allowed methods of a
+// preflight are looked up in the routes of the router the request is served
+// by. EnableCORS does that and also covers the OPTIONS requests that carry no
+// Access-Control-Request-Method.
+func CORS(options CORSOptions) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
+	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
+		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+			setCORSHeaders(w.Header(), r, options)
+			if isCORSPreflight(r) {
+				setCORSPreflightHeaders(w.Header(), r, options)
+				w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+				return
+			}
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// EnableCORS enables CORS on the mux with DefaultCORSOptions.
+func (mx *Mux) EnableCORS() {
+	mx.EnableCORSWithOptions(DefaultCORSOptions())
+}
+
+// EnableCORSWithOptions enables CORS on the mux with the given options. It
+// adds the CORS middleware and replaces the method not allowed handler by one
+// that also answers an OPTIONS request for a path that has no OPTIONS route
+// with the preflight headers and 204, and that lists the methods the path
+// does have in the Allow header of a 405.
+//
+// Like Use, it must be called before the routes of the mux are defined; on a
+// mux that already has routes the middleware wraps the whole mux instead.
+func (mx *Mux) EnableCORSWithOptions(options CORSOptions) {
+	cors := CORS(options)
+	if mx.inline || mx.handler == nil {
+		mx.Use(cors)
+	} else {
+		mx.handler = cors(mx.handler)
+	}
+	mx.MethodNotAllowed(corsMethodNotAllowed(options, mx.MethodNotAllowedHandler()))
+}
